messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: Unexpected result from stringr's str_replace_all
parts:
Hi All,

I'm cleaning a data set that is infested with odd combinations of extra spaces and periods scattered among people's names. I thought str_replace_all would fix it pretty easily, as it fixed many other problems in this data. But the result is surprising. Here's a simplified version. My goal is simply to remove the period-space combinations from this string vector:

> fruits <- c("one apple. ", ". two pears", "three.  bananas")

> str_replace_all(fruits, ". ", "")
[1] "onapple"       "twpears"       "three bananas"


Any ideas?

Thanks,
Bob

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected result from stringr's str_replace_all
parts:
Bob, 

You need to use the escape character and then again so you can get past R to the regex engine. `.` in regex generally means any character except \n, which is why it's matching more than you think. 

See here: 
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/6638072/escaped-periods-in-r-regular-expressions

Brandon
